posts.title: Fix left and right panels not opening in Liquid Glass mode
posts.details: Hovering the left or right screen edges now opens the Workspace Capsule / Left Panel and Control Center immediately when Liquid Glass mode is enabled.

report.where: ScreenBorder.qml, WallpaperBlur.qml and GlassFill.qml when Liquid Glass mode is active
report.wrong: ScreenFrame sat above the edge hover strips and WallpaperBlur's HoverHandler defaulted to blocking: true in Qt 6, swallowing pointer hover events before the edge triggers could fire.
report.changed: Moved ScreenFrame behind all edge triggers in ScreenBorder.qml and set blocking: false on the glass HoverHandlers in WallpaperBlur.qml, GlassFill.qml and ScreenBorder.qml.

posts.title: Thx for 30star
posts.details:
Anserin has reached 30 stars in just 10 days! I'm so happy that so many people are trying and using this shell.

I'll keep working hard to make Anserin as stable and great as possible — thank you so much for trusting and using my shell.

posts.title: 49% lower RAM at full 60 fps & automatic idle cleanup
posts.details:
Before: Anserin held 10 OpenGL windows (~552 MB PSS, 10 QSGRenderThreads, 40 Mesa GL threads), including 4 invisible 1x1 Qt/OpenGL border windows and 2 edge-hover windows, and panels kept cached images and hidden GPU resources after closing.

Now: A pure-CPU Wayland layer-shell helper (anserin-core reserve, ~0.55 MB PSS, 0 GL) replaces the 4 invisible border windows without touching monitor scale or mode, left/right edge triggers share ScreenBorder, Music bar mounts only while a track is active, and closing panels clears image/QML caches and hidden window GPU resources after 30 s — cutting idle RAM to ~281 MB PSS (-49%) while keeping the full 60 fps threaded render loop.

posts.title: Clean Reload shell without locking the screen
posts.details:
Before: Reload shell used in-process forceReload, which could leave Mesa and Qt heap fragmented across repeated reloads.

Now: Right-clicking Reload shell (or running anserin reload) cleanly restarts anserind in the background without locking the screen, reclaiming 100% of Mesa/Qt memory on every reload.

posts.title: Smart Home Control Center & faster pages
posts.details:
Before: Control Center used the board of small tiles and built all Settings pages at once (~616 ms pause on open).

Now: Control has a new Smart Home card layout with spring switches, sliders, smooth mouse-wheel and touchpad scrolling, and 14 per-page async loaders (opening ~3–6x faster, ~100–180 ms). Overview gets three expressive Wave Dials (brightness, volume, mic) and icon-only quick actions with water-wave fills while keeping the sleeping duck notification nest.

posts.title: Kinetic Light-Rail left panel & 72% faster open
posts.details:
Before: The left panel compiled all 9 pages together on its first open (~493 ms freeze) and paused 220 ms when expanding from the workspace capsule.

Now: The L-shaped frame carries a glowing fiber-optic light rail, morphing corner emblem and spring indicator. Each page compiles and loads lazily on demand, cutting first-open time from ~493 ms to ~138 ms (-72%) and capsule wait to 45 ms.

resources.ram: less than before (only opened pages load)

posts.title: Smart Music with Liquid Mercury Equalizer
posts.details:
A new Music style (Smart, replacing Ambient) matching Smart Weather, with Mirror and Theme tones, a spinning vinyl disc, synced lyrics, and a 10-band Liquid Mercury Wave GPU equalizer with Ball-Impact Cascade animations and stereo harp sound effects.

Pick it in Edit panel → Style → Music.

resources.cpu: ~8% of one core while EQ is open

posts.title: Floating Music bar with synced lyrics & Cava wave
posts.details:
An optional floating pill at the top or bottom of your screen showing the playing cover, auto-paginating synced lyrics (English and Thai), and a seamless 360° GPU wave hugging the capsule with zero corner seams. Click to open Music; uses zero RAM when turned off or idle.

Turn it on in Control Center → Control → Panel → Music.

posts.title: Minimal & Smart System Monitor styles
posts.details:
Two new RAM-friendly System Monitor styles: Minimal (Hardware Bento cards for CPU P/E cores, GPU/VRAM, RAM, Disk, Network, Power profile, Battery, Ping and Top-5 Processes) and Smart (smoked-glass HUD in Mirror and Theme tones). Polling stops as soon as the panel closes.

Pick them in Edit panel → Style → System.

posts.title: Claude Panel: Claude Code inside a collapsible overlay
posts.details:
Press Super + C (or right-click the desktop) to open a real Claude Code terminal with a liquid-wave GPU reveal, a corner dome with the waving Clawd mascot, and a side Studio rail showing live edited files/diffs, slash commands, recent sessions, model/effort switcher and context usage — without touching ~/.claude/settings.json.

Requires claude CLI and Qt 6 qmltermwidget. Also available standalone at github.com/lukpednoi/Claude-Panel.

posts.title: Flip Clock desktop widget
posts.details:
A 3D split-flap HH:MM:SS clock widget that flips each card only when its digit changes, using zero animation frames at rest.

Add it from Open Redactor → Clocks → Clock → Flip.

posts.title: Unified bouncy Open Redactor & Custom Lock Screen
posts.details:
Before: Open Redactor kept an empty left panel before picking a widget, clicking a style replaced instead of adding duplicates, and Custom Lock Screen still used the old horizontal strip with floating tools.

Now: Both editors share one clean layout. The left preview panel stays hidden until you pick a widget from the bottom bar, then springs out smoothly at 60 fps. Every click on a style card immediately adds a new widget (duplicates allowed with automatic offset), and the top toolbar stays clean above the canvas.

posts.title: 40% lower idle RAM without cutting features
posts.details:
Before: Anserin sat around ~632 MB PSS at rest because 11 overlays/popouts, wallpaper preloading, idle transition FBOs and helper daemons stayed resident even when never opened.

Now: Overlays and popouts load lazily with grace-unload, wallpaper FBOs and audio/inhibit helpers run only when needed, and the native core trims freed heap pages back to the OS — cutting idle Anserin PSS from ~632 MB to ~379 MB (-40%).

posts.title: Refreshed Anserin logo & balanced Soft Smart Home SFX
posts.details:
Before: UI sound effects were quiet and uneven across controls.

Now: Refreshed Anserin logo and expressive spring primitives, with normalized Soft Smart Home UI and stereo harp EQ sound effects played cleanly through anserin-core.

posts.title: Digital Wellbeing removed & Wallpapers moved to companion repo
posts.details:
Digital Wellbeing has been removed from Control Center to keep the shell lighter, and Launcher now runs automatically on demand.

The wallpaper pack (200 images and 11 videos) now lives in its own repository (github.com/lukpednoi/Anserin-Wallpapers, linked in README) so the main Anserin repo stays fast to clone and update.

posts.title: Fixed tiling recovery with string window IDs
posts.details: Fixed an issue where infinite-desktop and scrollable-tiling recovery could skip windows whose Hyprland address arrived as a string.

report.where: Infinite desktop and scrollable tiling layout recovery
report.wrong: Window addresses delivered as strings were not matched during recovery
report.changed: Recovery scripts now normalize and accept string window IDs cleanly

posts.title: UI Scale now follows your display settings
posts.details:
Control Center → Display no longer changes your monitor's scale. It now shows the scale and logical size your screen already uses.

Each monitor keeps the scale set in your compositor config (Hyprland, Niri or Sway), so Anserin fits every screen resolution without overriding it.

posts.title: Anserin's own engine under the hood
posts.details:
Before: system info, brightness, lock keys and Night light leaned on helpers from Serpantinum, and every click sound started its own player.

Now: Anserin has its own core. Sounds start in about 4 ms instead of 80 ms, wallpaper lists load small copies of your pictures (about 12x faster), video wallpapers get a real poster instead of a blank first frame, and wallpapers can sit in Images and Videos subfolders.

Nothing to set up: it builds itself the first time Anserin starts (cmake and a C++ compiler are needed; without them Anserin keeps its old ways).

posts.title: Gargantua: a black hole for your Network page
posts.details:
A new Network style. Your router sits inside a live black hole, with the Wi-Fi networks around you floating in its glow. Click one to connect.

Pick it in Edit panel → Style → Network. It has its own editor for colour, tilt and how the networks group.

posts.title: Radar: a calm map of the networks near you
posts.details:
A new Network style. The networks around you are drawn as a web of points around your router, with the one you use at the bottom and its power button beside it.

Pick it in Edit panel → Style → Network.

posts.title: Smart Weather: a sky that matches outside
posts.details:
A new Weather style, like a smart mirror. The whole page is a sky that follows the time of day and the weather now (rain, clouds, mist, snow, storms), with the hours and the next five days below.

Pick it in Edit panel → Style → Weather. Its editor lets you try any time and weather.

posts.title: Style editors use one simple bar
posts.details:
Before: a style's settings opened in a tall card beside the preview.

Now: the settings sit in one short bar above the preview, with the same buttons and sliders in every editor, so the preview stays big and in the middle.

posts.title: A heads-up before heavy styles
posts.details: Some styles use a lot more of your computer than others. Picking one of them (Gargantua, or Bubble in System) now shows a short warning with a before and after picture. Got it keeps the new style, Cancel puts the old one back.

posts.title: A new way to add widgets
posts.details:
Before: Open Redactor showed only a small bar over your desktop, and you added a widget without seeing it first.

Now: your desktop shrinks to the right with a soft bounce. Pick a group at the bottom, then a widget, and every style of it shows live on the left, two per row. Click one and it lands on your desktop. The selected widget's tools sit above it, and closing grows the desktop back.

posts.title: The old Bar popups and desktop menu are gone
posts.details:
The Volume popup, the classic Calendar and the Calendar Dashboard could only be opened from the old Bar, so they are removed. Volume, music and network live in Control Center and the left panel.

Right-clicking the desktop no longer has a hidden old menu behind it. Right-clicking a widget still opens its menu, and the desktop's actions are in the corner revolver.

posts.title: Control has one layout now
posts.details: Control Center → Control always uses the dial and cards. The older "classic" layout, and the Settings pages only it used, are removed. It could only be turned on by editing the settings file by hand.

posts.title: Update's tabs sit in the middle
posts.details:
Before: the Latest, All and Not installed buttons sat on the left, and the version and date were on a separate line under them.

Now: the buttons are in the middle, with the version on their left and the date on their right, all on one line.

posts.title: No more alerts for the version you already have
posts.details: Anserin could tell you a version was out when you already had it. Fixed.

report.where: Right after logging in or restarting Anserin
report.wrong: The update alert sometimes named the version you already had
report.changed: Anserin now waits until it knows which version you have before it compares

posts.title: See what's new in Update
posts.details:
Control Center → Update now lists every release: Latest, All, and Not installed.

When a new version is out, Anserin tells you once and can update itself with one click. It checks GitHub a minute after you log in and then every 6 hours.

Some new features will arrive turned off. Open one and press Turn on to try it, and Turn off to go back.

posts.title: The Default interface is gone
posts.details:
Anserin is now the only interface. The bar, the floating Quick Actions and the separate Settings window are removed, along with the switch between interfaces.

If you were still on the Default interface, Anserin moves you over once and keeps your settings.

posts.title: New installs start in Anserin
posts.details: A fresh install now opens the Anserin interface you see in the screenshots.

report.where: Right after installing, on the first start
report.wrong: Anserin opened the old Default interface with a bar, not the Anserin interface
report.changed: New installs start in Anserin, and the old interface is removed

posts.title: Anserin is out
posts.details:
The first public version of Anserin. It comes with the Anserin interface, the left panel with Bubble, Control Center on the right edge, the corner revolver, the duck and the Simple lock screen.

Install it with the installer, and update with anserin -up.
